concepts.why: The patient presents with painful oral erosions and whitish edematous lacy patches with erosions on the tongue and buccal mucosa, which are characteristic of mucous membrane pemphigoid, and the lingual biopsy shows epidermal acanthosis and fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane.
The patient has a thymoma, which is a key feature of Good syndrome, and also has recurrent infections and low IgG levels, which are consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient has a thymoma and a range of autoimmune symptoms, including oral erosions and a mediastinal mass, which are consistent with thymoma-associated multiorgan autoimmunity.
The patient has recurrent infections and low IgG levels, which are characteristic of common variable immunodeficiency.
